entries.note: Claims are mostly faithful (4 of 55 lean on context: C14 'automated categorization', C28 GPT-3.5 not in quote, C41 'this patch', C53 'it'), but the uncited sentence 'The two studies therefore disagree on whether length is a usable failure signal' is wrong (both cited sentences are R35; the disagreement is with R81/C54), and the GRL/42-requirements and SpecRover 'proposed rather than evaluated' sentences are unsupported. I3 generalizes from length to all surface trace features and I8 uses C46 (patterns often NOT reusable) as support; the experience-reuse/trace-memory literature named in the scope is absent and not flagged.

C25/C31 say R87 'calls [the harness] a structured form of context engineering' but the quote does not, and that claim carries the abstract and I4/I14; also C46 ('across the sources' from one source), C42 drops 'Anthropic's', C39/C40 add 'harness', and the uncited 'Another paper, by contrast...' sentence has no source. I7 says sources 'diverge' on C34/C45 while I17 says 'likewise'; practitioner literature and a separate account of agentic harnesses (the review's HeavySkill R30) are missing, and much text repeats the same claims.

Claims are largely faithful (C20 'such methods', C25 'its accuracy' and C48 'serving cost' lean on context), and the paper repeatedly and honestly says the user-named Shao et al. Context Language Models paper was not retrieved, so CLM is answered only as compression. The uncited 'no passage covers recursive language models on cost' contradicts C15/C34 and the C5 quote (comparable cost), and 'the compression line modifies or trains parameters' does not fit H2S/LongLLMLingua; interpretations are cautious, with I3 (Chained RLM 'sits between the two') the main stretch.
